### Why `Clause-②: no`, and why it survives a route not yet chosen

Two independent grounds, either sufficient:

1. ⭐ **`apps/console` is an application, ⛔ not a published contract face.** Clause ② 「只指已发布契约面」. Nothing in `apps/console/src/components/` ships as a package face.
2. ⭐ **The repair pulls an outlier back to an already-declared contract.** `file` is a declared field type whose control already exists and already works on the other renderer; `FormPage` re-spells the switch and drops it. 「拉回已声明契约不触它」 — this widens no accepted set, it stops a declared type from silently degrading.

⛔ The `no` is fenced, ⛔ not hopeful — see the scope fence below. If the route you find forces you outside `apps/console/`, that is a **stop-and-report**, not a re-declaration: a `no` cannot be revised on delivery.

### Premise re-taken by this seat on today's `origin/main` (⛔ not relayed)

The filing seat and triage both marked this 「⛔ Relayed, ⛔ not re-derived … Re-take it before writing」. Re-taken here, `origin/main` `98178b2`, 2026-09-20T23:25Z:

`apps/console/src/components/FormPage.tsx` carries a hand-rolled switch at roughly `:1501`–`:1591` whose arms are, in tree order: `textarea` / `paragraph` / `long_text` · `number` / `integer` / `decimal` / `currency` · `email` · `url` · `password` · `date` · `time` · `datetime` / `timestamp` · `boolean` / `toggle` / `checkbox` · `select` / `picklist` / `enum` · `radio`.

⇒ ⭐ **no `file` arm — the card's premise holds.** ⚠️ And the same reading says the card is not alone: `image`, `lookup` / `reference` and `percent` are also absent from that list. ⛔ Those line numbers are this seat's reading of one ref and are **stale by default** — re-derive them; they are a lead, ⛔ not a specification.

### ⛔ Scope fence — the deliverable is ONE arm plus a report

Triage split this card explicitly and this dispatch keeps the split:

- ✅ **In scope**: make a `file` field work on a `FormView` (the `/f/:slug` and `/forms/:name` routes), plus the uncapped enumeration the card calls step 1 — which arms `FormPage`'s switch handles versus what the shared resolver handles.
- ⛔ **Out of scope**: adding arms for the other absent types, and the consolidation question 「why there are two input switches at all」. That one moves a renderer's architecture ⇒ it is a decision-box card, ⛔ not this card's deliverable. Your enumeration is the evidence that card will be built on, so make it complete and write it into the report even though you are ⛔ not acting on it.

⚠️ Triage's own words, kept verbatim because they are the acceptance condition and ⛔ not a preference: 「adding a `file` arm to `FormPage`'s hand-rolled switch fixes today's symptom and **guarantees a fifth card**」. ⇒ the enumeration is not a footnote of this card, it is half of it.

### How to read the table

- **Population** is `@objectstack/spec/data`'s own `FieldType` enum, not a hand list.
- **FormPage arm** is parsed out of `FieldInput`'s `switch (field.type)` body; `yes` means a literal `case` spells that exact name.
- **shared resolver widget** is a RUNTIME read: `resolveFormWidgetType(t)` called against the BUILT `@object-ui/fields` (`packages/fields/dist/index.js`), so the alias table is included. ⚠️ A first pass of this table fell back to parsing `fieldWidgetMap`'s keys out of source when the import failed; that version reported ten types as "no dedicated widget" which the runtime read shows resolving through aliases (`toggle` to `boolean`, `json` to `code`, `secret` to `password`, `video`/`audio` to `file`, `tree` to `lookup`, `progress` to `slider`, `composite`/`record` to `object`, `repeater` to `grid`, `autonumber` to `auto_number`). The numbers below are the runtime ones.
- `text` appears in the "absent from FormPage" list and is the one member of it that is **correctly** served: the `default` arm IS a text input. So the count of types where the default arm is the WRONG control is **34**, not 35.
- ⛔ No arm was added for anything in this table except `file`.

### The three axes an arm list cannot see

The dispatch's assumption D asked whether the switch dispatches through a map, a lookup table or a nested helper that a `case` grep would miss. **It does not** — the parse reports zero non-`case` dispatch in the switch body, so the arm list is complete on the TYPE axis. It is incomplete on three others, and this is the part of step 1 the `file` symptom could never have produced:

1. **`widget`** — the spec declares `widget` as an optional string on a field; `packages/plugin-form/src/sectionFields.ts` carries `fd.widget` and `packages/components/src/renderers/form/form.tsx` resolves `f?.widget || f?.field?.widget || f?.type`. Three widget keys (`object-ref`, `filter-condition`, `recipient-picker`) are reachable ONLY that way. `FormPage` reads no `widget` key at all.
2. **Arity** — `mapFieldTypeToFormType('select', { multiple: true })` returns `field:multiselect`, a different component. This switch's `select` arm is single-value, so a declared multi-value picklist degrades here even though `select` "has an arm".
3. **Retirement** — `resolveFormWidgetType('owner')` returns `owner`, which the registry answers with a visible-refusal tombstone (objectui#4814). Here `owner` has no arm and the default renders a working text box.

⇒ a switch keyed on `type` alone cannot be brought level with the shared resolver by adding arms, however many are added. That is the measured form of triage's "guarantees a fifth card", and it is offered as the evidence base for the decision-box card, ⛔ acted on nowhere in PR objectui#10173.
